title: The cable that shrank the world
text: {{1}} 1866, news crossing the Atlantic travelled no faster than the ships that carried it: a letter posted {{2}} steamer could take ten days to arrive. The businessman Cyrus Field was determined to change {{3}}, and he spent twelve years and several fortunes trying. {{4}} five failed attempts, a durable cable was finally completed between Ireland and Newfoundland in 1866, and distance was instantly abolished as an obstacle {{5}} urgent business. Financial prices in London and New York moved so closely together {{6}} a market panic in either city could be felt in {{7}} other within hours. The ocean came to feel less like a wall than like a corridor, and the age of instant global news, {{8}} we now take for granted, had begun.

gaps.explanation: 'Before 1866' locates the period prior to the cable.
'By steamer' — the means of transport takes 'by'.
'Change it' — the pronoun refers to the slow news situation.
'After five attempts' — the completion came later.
'An obstacle to' — the fixed noun partnership.

gaps.hint: conjunction: so closely together ___ a panic
gaps.explanation: 'So … that' — degree followed by the result clause.

gaps.hint: article: felt in ___ other within hours
gaps.explanation: 'The other' — the second of the two named cities.
